pack.description: Vocabulary of anthropology and archaeology passages and talks: cultures, kinship, early humans and excavation.
pack.selection_note: Internal selection of terms that recur in introductory anthropology texts; this is not an official list and CEFR levels are author estimates.
pack.copyright_policy: Original content written for this app. No dictionary definition, ETS item or external word list was copied.

entries.definition: a set of actions performed in a fixed way, often as part of a ceremony
entries.example_academic: The ritual marked the moment at which a boy was accepted as an adult.
entries.example_spoken: Coffee before class is my morning ritual.

entries.definition: the fact of being related in a family, or the system of family relationships in a society
entries.example_academic: Kinship determined who could marry whom and who inherited land.
entries.example_spoken: There's a real sense of kinship among the exchange students.

entries.definition: an object made by people in the past that has historical interest
entries.example_academic: The artifacts recovered from the site include tools, beads and fragments of pottery.
entries.example_spoken: The museum has artifacts you can actually pick up.

entries.definition: belonging to the people, plants or animals that lived in a place first
entries.example_academic: Indigenous knowledge of local plants has guided several pharmaceutical discoveries.
entries.example_spoken: The course covers the indigenous languages of the region.

entries.definition: moving from place to place instead of living in one place all the time
entries.example_academic: Nomadic herders followed seasonal pastures across the plateau.
entries.example_spoken: He had a pretty nomadic childhood; his family moved every year.

entries.definition: belonging to or coming from the family members who lived long before you
entries.example_academic: The community was forced to leave its ancestral lands.
entries.example_spoken: They still live in the ancestral home.

entries.definition: a way of behaving that has existed for a long time among a group of people
entries.example_academic: The custom of exchanging gifts created lasting obligations between families.
entries.example_spoken: It's the custom here to take your shoes off.

entries.definition: the traditional stories, beliefs and customs of a community
entries.example_academic: Folklore preserves memories of events that written records ignore.
entries.example_spoken: According to local folklore, the lake has no bottom.

entries.definition: the state of having just enough food or money to stay alive
entries.example_academic: Subsistence farming left households vulnerable to a single failed harvest.
entries.example_spoken: Most families there live at subsistence level.

entries.definition: to bring animals or plants under human control so that they can live with or be grown by people
entries.example_academic: Dogs were domesticated long before the emergence of agriculture.
entries.example_spoken: People first domesticated wheat about ten thousand years ago.

entries.definition: to dig in the ground carefully in order to find old objects or buildings
entries.example_academic: Archaeologists excavated the site over five consecutive summers.
entries.example_spoken: They're excavating a Roman villa behind the library.

entries.definition: a place where people have come to live and built homes, especially for the first time
entries.example_academic: The earliest settlements appeared along rivers that flooded predictably.
entries.example_spoken: There was a small settlement here before the town was founded.

entries.definition: the act or ceremony of putting a dead body into the ground
entries.example_academic: Objects placed in the burial suggest a belief in life after death.
entries.example_spoken: The burial took place the day after the funeral service.

entries.definition: the line of family members from whom a person is descended
entries.example_academic: Property passed through the female lineage in this society.
entries.example_spoken: She can trace her lineage back four hundred years.

entries.definition: the passing of stories, history and knowledge from one generation to the next by speaking rather than writing
entries.example_academic: In the absence of writing, laws were preserved through oral tradition.
entries.example_spoken: We only know that story through oral tradition.

entries.definition: a social or religious rule that forbids a particular action or subject
entries.example_academic: Food taboos often serve to mark the boundary between one group and another.
entries.example_spoken: Talking about salaries is still a taboo in many offices.

entries.definition: the detailed study and description of the life of a particular group of people, usually based on living among them
entries.example_academic: Her ethnography of a fishing village is based on two years of fieldwork.
entries.example_spoken: For the assignment we have to read a full ethnography.

entries.definition: a member of the biological family that includes humans and their early relatives
entries.example_academic: The fossil belongs to a hominid that walked upright three million years ago.
entries.example_spoken: That skull is from a hominid, not a modern human.

entries.definition: tracing family relationships and inheritance through mothers rather than fathers
entries.example_academic: In matrilineal societies, a man's heirs are often his sister's children.
entries.example_spoken: Their clan system is matrilineal, so names come from the mother.

entries.definition: living in one place rather than moving around; also, involving a lot of sitting
entries.example_academic: The shift to a sedentary way of life allowed populations to store surplus grain.
entries.example_spoken: I have a very sedentary job, so I try to walk at lunch.

entries.definition: the belief that natural things such as animals, trees and rivers have a spirit
entries.example_academic: Animism attributes intention and awareness to rivers, mountains and storms.
entries.example_spoken: The film borrows a lot from Japanese animism.

entries.definition: the process of taking on the customs and ideas of another culture after long contact with it
entries.example_academic: Acculturation was most rapid among those who traded regularly with the newcomers.
entries.example_spoken: My accent changed as part of acculturation, I guess.

entries.definition: a person who is believed to be able to contact spirits and heal the sick
entries.example_academic: The shaman acted as healer, adviser and keeper of the group's history.
entries.example_spoken: In the documentary, the shaman prepares a drink from forest plants.

entries.definition: a ceremony or event that marks a person's move from one stage of life to another
entries.example_academic: Marriage functions as a rite of passage that redefines a person's obligations.
entries.example_spoken: Moving into a dorm is a rite of passage for most students.

entries.definition: the physical objects that a society makes and uses, studied as evidence of how its people lived
entries.example_academic: The material culture of the site suggests regular contact with coastal traders.
entries.example_spoken: You can learn a lot from material culture, like what people threw away.

entries.definition: the idea that a society's beliefs and customs should be understood by its own standards, not judged by those of another
entries.example_academic: Cultural relativism asks the researcher to suspend judgment while describing a practice.
entries.example_spoken: Cultural relativism doesn't mean you have to agree with everything.

entries.definition: walking on two legs
entries.example_academic: The shape of the pelvis indicates that the species was fully bipedal.
entries.example_spoken: Birds are bipedal too, if you think about it.

entries.definition: a person or animal that lives by searching for wild food rather than by farming
entries.example_academic: Foragers typically worked fewer hours than early farmers did.
entries.example_spoken: Bears are opportunistic foragers; they eat whatever they find.

entries.definition: a group of people who have spread from their original country to live in many other places
entries.example_academic: The diaspora maintained its language through schools and newspapers abroad.
entries.example_spoken: There's a big Lebanese diaspora in this city.
